claim_scope: One data change to the shipped JavaScript sink vocabulary, measured on NodeGoat. Detection only. No capability qualified: NodeGoat developed this analyser.
question: Does the untrusted-destination family ask about the outbound request a Node server actually makes?

design.bare_module_names: axios, got, needle, request, superagent, unirest, undici and fetch are the documented call form of their own module, and a bare token also covers every verb method through it: tokens match word-bounded against the callee, and axios is bounded inside axios.get. So axios.get and axios.post were dropped as subsumed, not as unwanted.
design.dotted_node_core: http and https stay dotted. Their namespace also holds createServer, and a bare token would have claimed every server a repository starts as an outbound request.
design.redirect_unchanged: The CWE-601 entry is untouched. res.writeHead with a Location header is a value-shaped redirect this arbiter cannot decide, and widening to writeHead would claim every response.

measured_on_nodegoat.token_matches_vendored: zero for every candidate, including the 13 vendored bundles under app/assets
measured_on_nodegoat.note: needle matches exactly one call, the research handler's request. redirect matches seven, of which six take a literal destination and are correctly not reported. The other clients do not appear in this repository at all, so NodeGoat shows the gap closing and cannot show these clients' noise.

control: tests/test_cpg_queries_compile.py::test_a_literal_destination_is_not_an_untrusted_destination builds a handler that calls axios.get with a literal and needle.get with req.query.url, and asserts the flow is reported for the tainted client only. It reads the shipped vocabulary rather than a copy, so removing the client fails the control. Seven Joern-gated query tests pass in the image.
limits: NodeGoat contains only one of the twelve clients, so eleven are declared on documentation, not measured.
A bare module token matches any call whose callee spells that module, including a same-named local variable.
Server-side redirects written as a Location header are still outside what this family asks.
